needed_assertion.statement: The normalization is finite flat; regular differentials on a common resolution extend to its reflexive relative dualizing module; finite duality specializes to Hom(C,O_K) and identifies coordinates with omega/dt at every split fibre point.
needed_assertion.objects: Normalization of an arithmetic projective line in a finite cover, common regular resolution, dualizing module, split fibre order C and differential evaluations.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: The arithmetic base is regular of dimension2; normalization is finite and normal, hence Cohen-Macaulay; the chosen fibre is split and etale.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Every regular differential extends to the reflexive dualizing module and specializes to an element of Hom(C,O_K).
needed_assertion.parameter_range: Finite covers in characteristic zero over rings of integers; no assumption that the normal surface is regular.
needed_assertion.uniformity: Finite projectivity allows duality to commute with the chosen base change.

needed_assertion.uniformity: The same L-prime is used for the factor and the isogeny theorem; no unbounded splitting extension is inserted.
needed_assertion.constants: hF(B)<=max(1,hF(J)+3g/2). Dimension2 isogeny degree <=(14^32 [L-prime:Q] max(1,log[L-prime:Q],hF(B)))^16; isogeny-height cost is one-half log degree.
needed_assertion.normalizations: Product additivity and Bost lower bound are in original stable normalization, including rank0 complement height0.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: A may be nonsimple and B may repeat a simple factor; choose by isogeny multiplicity. Do not use the superseded arbitrary-subvariety height inequality.
needed_assertion.limit_order: First replace J by the same-field low-height product, next choose B and bound its height using the complement, finally apply the dimension2 isogeny bound.
